unsupported_claims: key_fact 7 transposes K and V: it states 'turbo3-K + q8_0-V = 161.6 PPL'. In docs/experiment-asymmetric-kv.md (branch experiment/asymmetric-kv, commit d9e1090) the 161.6/2023 row is q8_0-K + turbo3-V, and the 'rot tensors not allocated when K is non-turbo' note only fits that row (K=q8_0). The reading simultaneously lists 'q8_0-K + turbo3-V CRASHED', but the doc marks that row BROKEN (PPL 161.6), while the CRASHED rows are turbo3-K + q8_0-V and turbo3-K + q4_0-V. So one combination is reported both as 161.6-BROKEN and as CRASHED, and the actual BROKEN combination is reported as crashed.

key_fact 10's gap-recovery numbers do not match the paper it cites. docs/papers/layer-aware-v-compression.md's 'Compression efficiency' table (lines 97-100) states 62% for Qwen2.5-7B and 43% for Qwen3.5-27B. The reading quotes 37% and 42%. Recomputing from the paper's own PPL table gives 37.3% and 42.5%, and docs/benchmarks.md line 28 prints 37% — i.e. the reading used benchmarks.md/arithmetic, not the cited paper's stated column, and did not flag that the paper's gap column is internally inconsistent with its own PPL table (62% vs 37%).

key_fact 9's 'Validated across 7 models (1.5B-104B), 3 weight quants, 3 backends (Metal/CUDA/HIP)' is the paper's abstract sentence reproduced as MEASURED, but the same paper §7 says 'Metal primary, CUDA/HIP secondary. Most experiments run on Apple Silicon Metal. CUDA and HIP results confirm the pattern but with fewer model/config combinations tested.' The '3 backends' framing overstates the CUDA/HIP depth.

reusable_assets calls scripts/turbo_hardware_diag.py a '2385-line diagnostic'. `wc -l` on main gives 2398 lines; 2385 is the repo's own self-report in docs/turboquant-plus-experiments.md line 137, so it is a source claim the reader did not measure.

The summary labels d9e1090 (asymmetric-kv) and b96d0d1 (moe-aware-gating) as branch 'tips'. The actual tips are the merge commits d502cd4 and 7b3124a (both 2026-03-25); d9e1090/b96d0d1 are the doc commits underneath. key_fact 3 lists the correct merge tips, so the reading contradicts itself.

failures_and_lessons attributes the 16K dilution figure '-0.006 PPL' to 'Boundary V' generally. In docs/papers/layer-aware-v-compression.md the -0.006 is specifically the 4+4-vs-turbo2 advantage at 16K (Addendum Part 2); no 16K LA-V7 (2+2) number is given.
errors_found: Omission of the production corruption correction in docs/papers/asymmetric-kv-compression.md §7 (lines 251-252, 2026-04-02): @sjoerdmaessen found asymmetric q8_0-K/turbo3-V produces corrupt output (literal U+003F '?' characters) on Qwen3.5-122B while symmetric turbo3/turbo3 worked, traced to V operations gated on k->type (issue #42, fix branch fix/turbo-v-unpad-gate unmerged). The reading elevates q8_0-K + turbo-V as the headline recommendation ('the dominant reusable finding') and never mentions this. This is the single most load-bearing omission and it directly undercuts hypothesis seed 5.

Omission of the contradicting independent result in the same paper the reading cites: docs/papers/asymmetric-kv-compression.md line 247-248 (@Madreag, CUDA, 4 GPUs, 2026-04-01) reports 'V type dominates PPL' and 'K=turbo3/V=turbo3 (6.7251) approximately equals K=q8_0/V=turbo3 (6.6885) ... K precision matters less than V precision ... asymmetric is not needed on Q6_K+ weights'. The reading presents K-precision dominance as settled and never notes this direct counter-result.
K/V transposition in key_fact 7 (detailed above): the 161.6 BROKEN row is q8_0-K + turbo3-V, not turbo3-K + q8_0-V, and the q8_0-K + turbo3-V combination is mislabeled CRASHED.

Gap-recovery mismatch and unflagged source-internal inconsistency: the reading cites docs/papers/layer-aware-v-compression.md for 37%/42% while that paper's own gap column says 62%/43%; the 62% is arithmetically wrong against the paper's PPL table (37.3%).
Minor factual slips: '2385-line' vs actual 2398 (`wc -l`); branch 'tip' mislabel (d9e1090/b96d0d1 vs merge tips d502cd4/7b3124a).

The reading flags docs/benchmarks.md's '64L' MoE layer count as conflicting with the paper's 40L/10-KV metadata, but misses the same table's second conflict: docs/benchmarks.md line 30 gives Qwen3.5-27B Dense '36L', while the paper's verified metadata says 64 total layers / 16 KV. Both rows are wrong in benchmarks.md; the reading caught only one.
missing_angles: The corruption correction and its lesson (speed-only benchmarks masked garbage output; discovered only by reading chatbot responses) is directly on-theme for the town's stated moral of 'KNOWLEDGE and WISDOM extracted per token spent, failures included', and it is the failure that most bears on the reading's recommended config.

The independent-validation addendum in docs/papers/layer-aware-v-compression.md (2026-03-31, @sztlink) found that protecting boundary K layers did NOT reduce the gap — the gap grew more negative — because boundary layers already compress better (layer-0 K norm 146.8 vs 20-40 middle) and are near-Gaussian after normalization. That makes the 'last N layers are sensitive' effect distributional (K norms) rather than positional, which undercuts hypothesis seed 3's premise that fixing raw-index to KV-layer ordinal will change the measured recovery by a large margin.

The repo's own docs/papers/attn-rotation-and-ppl-artifact.md demonstrates that corpus PPL ranks KV-quant configs backwards on gemma-class instruct models and recommends KLD-vs-fp16-KV instead (ggerganov's own PR #21038 comment: 'track the KLD rather than PPL'). Every one of the reading's six hypothesis seeds uses PPL as the arbiter; the reader lists 'corpus-KLD' as a refract axis but never flags that PPL may not be a valid oracle or recommends KLD in the seeds.

No CPU turbo kernel exists. All quality and speed numbers are Metal (plus community CUDA/HIP PPL); the C++ implementation lives in a separate fork with zero .cpp/.cu/.metal in this repo (verified: 0 of 245 tracked files). The Python reference (turboquant/kv_cache.py) is a prototype whose norm granularity differs from the llama.cpp codec, so its fidelity as a CPU surrogate for the branch's PPL claims is unestablished. The seeds repeatedly say 'if a CPU build supports TURBO_LAYER_ADAPTIVE' when no such CPU build exists — the reading treats this as a conditional rather than the headline blocker.

The town's named target is Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M. Qwen is exactly the family where the repo reports symmetric turbo is catastrophic AND where the asymmetric rescue was later reported to corrupt output. The reading states the universal 'K is everything' rule but never connects the target model to the sensitive/corrupt family, which is the decision-relevant fact for this box.

Cross-source link the reader did not make: the sibling source bonsai2-small-gpu references a 'qwen 3.8 mtp head', the likely referent for the unresolved 'qwen3.8 50b' id the town asked to resolve; the tq-exp-structure reading does not point at it.
strongest_seed: Seed 1 (K-precision dominance holds for tiny CPU models <=3B Q4_K_M: q8_0-K + 2-3-bit V costs <5% PPL while compressing K is catastrophic). Highest knowledge-per-token on CPU: it is the foundational fact that decides whether KV compression is viable on the town's tiny models and where to spend bits; it is cheaply falsifiable in 1-3 CPU-hours with the NumPy reference or llama.cpp CPU -ctk q8_0 -ctv turbo2 and llama-perplexity; and the repo has only the catastrophic symmetric data at 1.5B (PPL 8,641+) with no asymmetric rescue measured below ~1.5B, so a positive or negative result is genuinely new and transfers directly to the CPU-only box. (Runner-up: seed 4, Boundary V on a tiny pure-attention model — also cheap and CPU-testable, but a narrower policy effect than the core K/V bit-allocation question.)
weakest_seed: Seed 5 (asymmetric mixed K/V validated end-to-end on the RTX 2070S only if llama.cpp CUDA kernels have q8_0 x turbo instantiations). It is GPU-bound and therefore off the town's CPU-only aim; the repo's C++ lives in a separate, Metal-first fork, so the likely outcome is 'no CUDA kernels', which is engineering status rather than transferable knowledge; and its premise rests on the asymmetric recommendation that the cited paper's own §7 reports can emit corrupt output. Even a positive result buys little for the CPU town. (Seed 2, layer-adaptive CPU transfer, is also weak: it cannot actually be tested without a CPU turbo build, so its Python emulation measures reconstruction error, not the claimed PPL gap.)
